name: SQUID migration self-sale uses manipulable minimum output
summary: SquidTokenSwap.sellSwappedTokens is public and derives its minimum output from the same PancakeSwap reserves its trade consumes. An attacker repeatedly trades around the SQUID v1-to-v2 conversion and these treasury-funded sales, controlling both legs of the spot quote and extracting WBNB. The nominal 5% slippage check has no independent price reference.

loss.notes: 167.305316006695072569 WBNB extracted across six transactions on April 8 and April 14, 2024. Each component is the combined WBNB depletion of the SQUID v1/WBNB and v2/WBNB pools after all same-transaction WBNB inputs, including attacker-supplied principal. Internal swaps between the two pools cancel. The first two transactions pay 5 WBNB each to an external flash lender, retained in gross loss. SQUID reserve transfers, intermediate purchases and burns are not valued again. Each recurrence uses a preceding BNB/USD quote. Gas, builder payments and later recovery do not reduce the measurement.

ageReset.description: The direct runtime fixes token addresses, router and spot-quote validation from creation. One-time enableSwap and address blacklisting gate exposure without changing that pricing logic.

sources.note: Reviewed anchor, root cause, loss, artifact identity and complete age history. Etherscan V2 getsourcecode for the target returns verified contracts/SquidV1toSquidV2TokenSwap.sol, contract SquidTokenSwap. swapTokens(uint256), selector 0xfe784eaa, exchanges equal raw quantities of SQUID v1 and v2. sellSwappedTokens(uint256), selector 0xe4defe8e, spends up to 500000 v1 per call and burns its v2 proceeds. getMinOut quotes v1 -> WBNB -> v2 via the immutable router, then multiplies the live quote by 95/100. The earlier summary claiming zero minimum output was incorrect. Source-1 callTracer executes four conversions and 328 successful treasury sales around attacker swaps in both pools. The quote and router minimum are satisfied under reserves moved by the attacker in the same transaction, rather than bounding execution against an independent value. The other five transactions repeat this feedback loop, later using fresh callback contracts to evade address blacklisting. Source-5 is direct CREATE by the declared creator at 36844517:54. Code is empty at 36844516, and its 6965-byte hash matches at creation, 37672969 and source-1 prestateTracer. Verified source has no upgrade, delegatecall, destruction or mutable token/router/price-parameter path. Source-6 calls enableSwap at 37659167:106. Slot 6 changes from zero at 37659166 to one at 37659167 and remains one before the exploit. This one-time gate changes reachability of the original unsafe spot-quote logic. Blacklisting and inventory counters also change exposure, without supplying a trusted price. Deployment is the latest code or causal configuration reset. For first-use coverage, scan target Swap(address,uint256,uint256) logs from deployment through block 125539643 in 100000-block intervals: 55 logs in 26 transactions. Independently scan SQUID v1 0x87230146e138d3f296a9a77e497a2a83012e9bc5 Transfer logs with topic1 equal to the padded target over the same range in 1000000-block intervals: 999 transfers in 15 transactions. The union is source-14. Every successful migration emits Swap, and every successful treasury sale transfers v1, so these cover both loss-bearing paths. Review all union receipts and callTracers. Six transactions combine repeated conversion, price-moving pool swaps and treasury sales. The remaining transactions are direct single-function EOA migrations or sales, without the atomic feedback loop. Before source-1, trace_filter toAddress=[target], 37659167..37682970 in 100-block intervals, count=10000, independently confirms no earlier internal attack. It returns 1070 frames in 18 transactions. Two extra attack attempts, 0xb10ef979e2c62004ff3742f5038291b2dd9e50721022abf388e9a0130478626b and 0x0044f7372e7ed7a8e73fe8bd9b68901ada4ff0affdad94c0d5b03e54fa015ee9, have receipt status zero and no logs. Before enablement, the irreversible gate is false and both paths revert. Loss uses the migration reserve plus SQUID v1/WBNB pool 0x683c425d917e8fef34c8bbbeab57246dd2a8b718 and v2/WBNB pool 0x009578c91568cce4c174fd77b33569d6dc82b7b5 as one victim system. Sum WBNB Transfer amounts from these pools minus amounts to them in each source-7 receipt. Their intermediate WBNB transfers cancel, every attacker WBNB input is credited, and all attacker SQUID inputs were acquired from this same system. This measures the scarce asset actually extracted, avoiding a spot mark on illiquid SQUID inventory. In source-1, the v2 pool loses 172.413575462181218876 WBNB while the v1 pool gains 21.565604043268262581, yielding 150.847971418912956295 WBNB. The attacker retains 145.847971418912956295 after a 5-WBNB external financing fee. The second transaction likewise pays 5 WBNB to that lender. Neither fee is deducted.
